decisions.reason: Even with no recent standalone website visibility, this capability is close to the firm's core authentication and secure-communication offer, so management would likely keep it as long as results are not clearly below aspiration levels.

Because mobile signing supports the firm's move toward app-based interactions and online contract execution, boundedly rational management would usually retain it, likely as part of a broader solution bundle.

This architecture-level offering is deeply tied to the firm's core security know-how and platform position, so its lower visibility is more likely to mean integration than failure warranting withdrawal.

A hardware token is the least aligned with the firm's app- and ecosystem-oriented trajectory, and after several years without visible traction it would likely fall below aspiration and be cut to free resources.

Compliance-focused security remains a good fit with the firm's regulated customer needs and technical capabilities, so management would tend to continue it unless niche demand has clearly disappointed.
